function_analysis: Unchanged: lower the mean wall shear at cruising speed versus a clean foul-release coating, biocide-free fouling control, 3-5 year durability (fender/cleaning abrasion is the main killer of soft coatings), no large consumption, hull-scale application. Lessons so far: soft graded layers give strong fouling-release gains but no credible drag gain and are fragile; hard surfaces are durable but release fouling poorly. Architected structures could decouple surface toughness from overall compliance.

requirements.name: low_friction_drag
requirements.criterion: Reduces the mean wall shear stress / frictional resistance at cruising speed versus a clean, standard foul-release hull coating.

requirements.name: non_toxic_antifouling
requirements.criterion: Prevents fouling settlement or makes it release easily without releasing biocides, heavy metals or other toxic substances into the sea.

requirements.name: multi_year_seawater_durability
requirements.criterion: Keeps its function and adhesion for at least 3-5 years in seawater (hydrolysis, abrasion, UV at the waterline, cleaning).

requirements.name: low_consumption_operation
requirements.criterion: Needs no continuous supply of material or energy that is large compared with the fuel it saves, and no frequent reapplication.

requirements.name: hull_scale_applicability
requirements.criterion: Can be applied to large steel hull areas with dry-dock methods at a cost comparable to premium hull coatings.

mechanism_classes_considered: architected_lattice (membrane over a compliant septa lattice: structural rather than material compliance)
electrostatic_field (checked against Debye screening and ohmic losses in seawater)
analogues_considered: Cuttlebone: thin lamellae held apart by wavy septa, a chambered lattice with tunable stiffness
Kramer's dolphin-inspired coatings: rubber membrane over stubs and viscous fluid
Nilas: thin elastic ice crust forming on grease ice/slush
Electric rays and weakly electric fish (field generation in conductive water)

candidates.title: Cuttlebone-septa membrane lattice skin
candidates.summary: A tough 0.3 mm silicone-polyurethane membrane spans a 2 mm high lattice of thin, wavy septa (cell size 2 mm) copied from cuttlebone; the cells are filled with a soft, water-swollen gel. Compliance is set by the septa geometry and membrane tension instead of by a very soft surface material, so the surface can be tough enough for fenders and cleaning while the structure stays as compliant as a soft foul-release coating.

back_of_envelope.quantity: Reduction of mean wall shear at 7 m/s versus a clean standard silicone foul-release coating
back_of_envelope.formula: As for all passive compliant walls: cell natural frequency f = (1/2L)*sqrt(T/m') with T = 50 N/m, m' = rho*h = 1100*3e-4 = 0.33 kg/m2 (plus added water mass ~rho_w*L/pi = 0.65 kg/m2), L = 2 mm -> f ~ 1.8 kHz, above the near-wall burst band (~300 Hz); DNS/experiments give 0-few % only at matched tuning, mistuned -> ~0-1%; take 0.5%. Main benefit: fouling release with a tough surface.

candidates.main_risk: Cell-scale surface waviness under pressure (membrane dimpling) can act as roughness or excite flutter, and the septa-membrane joints fatigue and let water into the cells.
candidates.novelty_vs_known: Closest: Kramer's stub-supported membrane coatings (1960s) and honeycomb cores (textbook). Adapted: cuttlebone-like wavy septa (bending-dominated, tunable, damage-tolerant) filled with gel, used to decouple surface toughness from compliance for a biocide-free foul-release coating rather than for drag alone.
candidates.baseline: Clean, standard silicone foul-release hull coating (~0.3 mm, E ~ 1 MPa) at 7 m/s
candidates.inspiration_source: Cuttlebone of Sepia officinalis: lamellae separated by thin, wavy septa
candidates.physical_mechanism: The surface membrane under tension T spans cells of size L and rests on an effective elastic foundation k (septa bending plus gel), so the steady deflection w(x) across a cell under a surface load p obeys T w'' - k w = -p with fixed edges at the septa. The mean deflection per load gives the surface compliance that sets fouling-release stress (Kendall) and the local stiffness seen by near-wall pressure fluctuations.

parameters.name: cell_size
parameters.justification: Cuttlebone chamber spacing ~0.2-1 mm scaled to hull coating build.

parameters.name: membrane_thickness
parameters.justification: Tough silicone-PU skin thickness similar to a standard topcoat.

parameters.name: membrane_tension
parameters.justification: Pre-tension from cure shrinkage (~0.1 MPa x 0.3 mm = 30-60 N/m).

parameters.name: foundation_stiffness
parameters.justification: Gel in 2 mm cells: k ~ G_gel/h ~ 1e5/2e-3 = 5e7 Pa/m.

parameters.name: surface_load
parameters.justification: Near-wall pressure fluctuation amplitude p' ~ 2.5 tau_w.

parameters.name: adhesion_work_surface
parameters.justification: Tough silicone-PU skin, slightly higher than pure PDMS.

candidates.title: Nilas-crust over slush-gel damped skin
candidates.summary: Like young sea ice, where a thin elastic nilas crust forms on top of grease-ice slush, a 0.15 mm tough, low-surface-energy silicone-PU crust (G ~ 0.5 MPa) covers a 2.5 mm soft, lossy gel (G ~ 60 kPa, tan delta ~ 1) that grades into a stiff base. The crust takes abrasion and raises the effective surface wave speed (bending stiffness), removing the hydroelastic instability of the bare gel, while the gel below keeps the coating compliant for easy fouling release.

back_of_envelope.quantity: Reduction of mean wall shear at 7 m/s versus a clean standard silicone foul-release coating
back_of_envelope.formula: Direct drag effect as for the parent: dissipated power ~ pi*tan_delta*p'^2*C*f ~ 0.02 W/m2 << 126 W/m2 near-wall production -> ~0.1-0.3%; take 0.3%. Series compliance C = t_crust/G_crust + C_gel = 1.5e-4/5e5 + ~1.1e-8 = 1.1e-8 m/Pa, so fouling release stays ~3x easier than standard foul release even with the crust.

candidates.main_risk: The crust/gel interface delaminates under repeated impacts because the gel has low cohesive strength, and a cut crust exposes the fragile gel.
candidates.novelty_vs_known: Closest: the grease-ice parent and commercial two-layer foul-release systems. New: a thin tough crust over a thick dissipative gel, which fixes the parent's two killer risks (abrasion and hydroelastic waves) without losing compliance; still honest that drag gain is negligible.
candidates.baseline: Clean, standard silicone foul-release hull coating (~0.3 mm, E ~ 1 MPa) at 7 m/s
candidates.inspiration_source: Nilas (thin elastic sea-ice crust) forming on grease ice/frazil slush
candidates.physical_mechanism: Series of a thin stiff crust and a thick graded soft gel under surface traction; the crust spreads concentrated loads (fender, brush) over a larger gel area and carries abrasion, the gel sets the overall compliance. Steady model: 1D shear deformation through the layered/graded stack under a surface traction, giving surface compliance and hence Kendall release stress; stability judged by crust bending wave speed.

parameters.name: gel_surface_shear_modulus
parameters.justification: Soft lossy gel under the crust (crust carries the flow loads).

candidates.infeasibility_reason: Seawater screens static fields within the Debye length (~0.4 nm), so a mm-scale electric field can only be sustained by an ohmic current (sigma ~ 5 S/m: ~50 W/m2 for 100 V/m over 1 mm, comparable with the entire friction power density of ~126 W/m2) that electrolyses seawater into chlorine/hypochlorite, violating both the energy balance and the non-toxic requirement; no electrostatic mechanism at this scale can lower wall shear.
